rv.q: Even if the execution isn’t flawless, Pretty Perfect Lives is the kind of ambitious, imaginative theater we need as we stand on the cusp of the metaverse and consider taking the plunge.
Tarlton's work is not without promise. As a social critique of people who are surgically attached to their smartphones, it is somewhat spot-on.
His play is simply more enjoyable when it’s making the audience laugh than when it’s making them think.

cn.t: Critics find this timely exploration of influencer culture and digital addiction raises relevant questions, but the execution doesn't fully deliver on its promising premise about modern tech obsession.
